newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end off lows but market bearish.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end off lows but market bearish.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended well off their session lows Tuesday, with locals caught by a round of short covering, but sentiment remained bearish after gold bullion saw new three year lows early in the day.
"The market remains confidently short, operating under protection of rumored central bank and producer selling," Chase Manhattan New York managing director Dinsa Mehta said.
"We suspect there may have been a central bank sale in the past month and there has been some scattered selling by producers," he said.
"The currency market is also a factor, with the U.S. dollar strong and volatility rising," he noted.

"Gold's historic and implied volatilities are also up off the record lows seen earlier this year, with at-the-money implied volatilities in nearby active months near eight percent, up about 1.75 percentage points in recent weeks."

COMEX February gold ended down 50 cents at $370.40 an ounce, after seeing a new life-of-contract low at $367.70 an ounce early in the day. Total estimates volume in gold futures was solid at 53,000 lots, traders said.
Spot gold in the bullion market ended quoted $368.40/368.90 an ounce, after gold fixed in London Tuesday afternoon at $367.40 an ounce, its lowest level since November 1993.
Gold has been in a long term downtrend from five year highs at $417.70 seen in February 1996.

Fears of European central bank sales, in preparation for the single European currency in 1999, have weighed on the market most of the year, after sales sales by the central banks of Belgium, Holland and Canada, analysts said.
On November 24 even the Switzerland, which has a quasi-gold standard, indicated it could consider selling gold.

The Swiss National Bank's chief legal counsel said the Federal Council of Switzerland was considering a proposal to remove the constitutional obligation to maintain gold stocks worth 40 percent of the Swiss currency in circulation and was looking at the possibility of selling part of its gold.
"We think this (Swiss) decision is a long term bear point for gold because it means more and more central banks will consider mobilizing their reserves," Arnold said.
The strength of U.S. stock and bond markets has also removed the incentive for investors to buy gold, while currency movements have also been a factor, analysts said.
"There looks to be an inverse relationship between the U.S. dollar and gold right now," Refco New York analyst Tim Porter said.
The U.S. dollar saw a 23 month high against the deutschemark Tuesday, after seeing a 42 month high against yen in early November.
The strength of the dollar has depressed demand in domestic currencies in Asia in particular, analysts said.

"Gold and silver demand from India has been slowing down sharply over the last six to eight weeks with the Bombay Bullion Market Association speaking of a 20 percent fall in gold demand during the recent Hindu Festival of Lights," Merrill Lynch analyst Ted Arnold said.

Strength in the Australian dollar and a partial recovery in the South African rand, lowering the price of gold in those countries, has led to reports of hedging by gold miners in those countries also, analysts said.

On the charts, next support for gold looks to be around $360 and then $350, analysts said, but a bounce is possible soon, with the spot gold's standard nine-day RSI (relative strength indicator) looking oversold at 15 percent and COMEX February gold's nine-day RSI at 16 percent, traders said.
The spot gold/silver ratio slipped to 77.07 at the close from 78.50 Monday as silver recovered further than gold in late trade.
COMEX March silver ended up 10.3 cents at $4.845 an ounce, after seeing a new contract low at $4.710 intraday. Total estimated silver futures volume was 14,000 lots.
NYMEX January platinum ended up 30 cents at $376.00 an ounce, after earlier seeing a new contract low at $373.10.
NYMEX March palladium closed down 60 cents at $117.25 an ounce, after seeing a new contract low at $116.60.
--Clive McKeef, New York Commodities Desk, +1-212-859-1641; email: clive.mckeef@reuters.com
